# PLAN — iteration 2

## Current state assessment

Iteration 1 passed behavior, timing, and verification but was rejected because its top-local `clean`, `tracked_value`, and 3-bit `count` implementation matched the timing-feasible incumbent at 4 LUTs and 5 FFs. The wrapper and frozen child together already meet timing at WNS 0.731 ns and WHS 0.126 ns, so this iteration must improve the LUT/FF objective while preserving closure.

## Hypothesis

Removing the separate tracked-value register and counting consecutive samples where `noisy` differs from `clean` should preserve the 8-cycle debounce behavior while reducing state from 5 FFs to 4, giving a strict FF improvement if LUT use stays at 4.

## Instruction for generator

Replace the child instance with top-local `clean` state and a 3-bit saturating counter; do not add a tracked-value register. On synchronous active-high reset, clear both; otherwise reset the counter when `noisy == clean`, and when `noisy != clean`, increment it until its prior value is 7, then update `clean` to `noisy` and clear the counter. Retain `// @latency 0`, the exact top interface, registered output behavior, and the existing clock; verify interrupted runs, both input levels, and reset against the unchanged testbench and all routed timing and metric gates.
